module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1090

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1090](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1090)
- [Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos1090

/--
Let $k\geq 3$. Does there exist a finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, in any $2$-colouring of $A$, there exists a line which contains at least $k$ points from $A$, and all the points of $A$ on the line have the same colour?

Erdős [Er75f] says Graham and Selfridge proved the answer is yes when $k=3$. Hunter has observed that, for sufficiently large $n$, a generic projection of $[k]^n$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$ has this property, by the Hales-Jewett theorem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1090.lean"]
theorem erdos_1090 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ (hk : 3 ≤ k),
    ∃ (A : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∀ (C : A → Fin 2),
      ∃ (S : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)), ∃ (hSA : S ⊆ A),
        Collinear ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) ∧ S.card ≥ k ∧
          (∀ y ∈ A, y ∈ affineSpan ℝ (S : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)) → y ∈ S) ∧
          ∃ c, ∀ x (hx : x ∈ S), C ⟨x, hSA hx⟩ = c := by
  sorry

end Erdos1090

reformulations.difference: Lean represents the line by a collinear finite subset S ⊆ A, requiring every point of A in affineSpan ℝ S to belong to S. It also restricts k to k ≥ 3, whereas the original paper says 'for every k'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since |S| ≥ k ≥ 3, S contains distinct points p and q. Mathlib's Collinear.affineSpan_eq_of_ne identifies affineSpan ℝ S with the genuine line through p and q. The subset and saturation conditions therefore give S = A ∩ line(p,q), so the color condition applies to every point of A on that line. Conversely, given a qualifying line L, take S = A ∩ L; it satisfies all the Lean conditions. Restricting the threshold to k ≥ 3 loses nothing: a witness for max(3,k) also works for k. Both the witness-level equivalence and the full quantified equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the sorry-backed problem theorem.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry, Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) 103 (1975), 99–108, §4, especially p. 106: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-25.pdf
Checked-out repository: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, PROOFS.md, FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean, and FormalConjecturesUtil/Attributes/Basic.lean.
review.notes: All declarations in the file were checked (there is one theorem). Boundary checks establish that empty or undersized A cannot be witnesses, that coloring functions always exist, and that for collinear A the saturation condition genuinely requires all of A to be monochromatic. The public database records 1090 as 'proved (Lean)', consistent with research solved and answer(True). The cited proof has exactly the required RHS; after tactic-only compatibility edits from its stated Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 to the sandbox's v4.33.1, it compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Direct access to erdosproblems.com/1090 and its forum was blocked by HTTP 403; the mathematical comparison used the cited original paper, with status corroborated by the accessible database and formal proof.
